body:
## Connections

Related to #9818 (`[meta] GPU memory allocation issues`). Brings DX12 to parity with Vulkan's `wgpu-hal/src/vulkan/memory.rs`.

## Description

`wgpu-hal/src/vulkan/memory.rs` separates `gpu_allocator` into `General` and `Transient` pools using `AllocationSizes::transient()` (`min_* / 4`) so that:
1. Short-lived resources (`MemoryFlags::TRANSIENT` staging buffers and compactable acceleration structures) do not share heap blocks with long-lived resources (preventing transient upload spikes from being pinned by persistent buffers/textures).
2. The last retained host block for staging uploads is 4× smaller (**16 MiB** instead of **64 MiB** under `MemoryHints::Performance`).

Previously, `wgpu-hal/src/dx12/suballocation.rs` ignored `desc.memory_flags` and `desc.allow_compaction`, placing all DX12 resources into a single `gpu_allocator::d3d12::Allocator`. As a result, every DX12 application using `MemoryHints::Performance` reserved 48 MiB more host memory than Vulkan (`[128 MiB, 64 MiB] = 192 MiB` vs `[128 MiB, 16 MiB] = 144 MiB`), and short-lived staging buffers could share blocks with persistent mapped buffers.

This PR mirrors `wgpu-hal/src/vulkan/memory.rs` in `wgpu-hal/src/dx12/suballocation.rs`:
- Adds `MemoryPool::{General, Transient}` and holds separate `general` and `transient` `Mutex<gpu_allocator::d3d12::Allocator>` instances (`gpu_allocator::d3d12::Allocator::new` creates zero heaps until first allocation).
- Routes buffers and textures via `MemoryPool::from_memory_flags(desc.memory_flags)` and acceleration structures via `desc.allow_compaction` (exact parity with Vulkan).
- Stores the originating `MemoryPool` on `AllocationInner::Placed` so `free_resource` returns allocations to the same pool.
- Merges both pools in `Allocator::generate_report()` with adjusted allocation index ranges (matching Vulkan).
- Uses the pool's `AllocationSizes` in `error_if_would_oom_on_resource_allocation`.
- Updates `AllocationSizes::transient()` in `wgpu-hal/src/lib.rs` to round `min_* / 4` up to multiples of `4 MiB` (clamped `>= 4 MiB`) so `MemoryHints::MemoryUsage` and `Manual` sizes match `gpu-allocator`'s 4 MiB alignment without warning or OOM-budget discrepancy, updates the `dead_code` cfg guard to `not(any(dx12, vulkan))`, and adds a unit test.
- Enables `Backends::DX12` in the existing permanent GPU regression test `TRANSIENT_BUFFERS_RELEASE_MEMORY_BLOCKS` (`tests/tests/wgpu-gpu/transient_memory.rs`).

## Isolated A/B Benchmark Results

- **Environment**: Windows 11 (`Microsoft Windows [Version 10.0.26300.10075]`), Intel Core Ultra 7 155H, Intel Arc Integrated GPU (UMA, DX12 driver `31.0.101.5328`), `rustc 1.100.0`, `--release`.
- **Isolation & Methodology**: Unmodified `trunk` (`60cef2be`) vs this PR (`22827ee2`) **alone**, both using unmodified `gpu-allocator 0.28.0` (no `#11129` or `gpu-allocator#323` applied). Strictly sequential, alternating single-process runs: `N=5` trials across all 11 DX12 workloads/hints, plus `N=10` reverse-interleaved (`AB/BA`) runs on `repeated_uploads` and `small_gui` (marked `*`) to average out bimodal Intel iGPU DVFS clock-state transitions (`~240` vs `~440 us`) on short submit+poll loops. Medians and `(min–max)` ranges are reported across runs; GPU pass durations use hardware `Features::TIMESTAMP_QUERY`.
- **Reproducible harness & raw data**: [`simzy39/winit-wgpu-repro-benchmarks/wgpu-mem-bench`](https://github.com/simzy39/winit-wgpu-repro-benchmarks/tree/main/wgpu-mem-bench) | [`results/wgpu-11130/summary.md`](https://github.com/simzy39/winit-wgpu-repro-benchmarks/blob/main/results/wgpu-11130/summary.md) | [`raw/` (110 JSONs)](https://github.com/simzy39/winit-wgpu-repro-benchmarks/tree/main/results/wgpu-11130/raw) | [`raw-abba10/` (40 JSONs)](https://github.com/simzy39/winit-wgpu-repro-benchmarks/tree/main/results/wgpu-11130/raw-abba10)

### DX12 Memory, CPU Latency/Throughput, and Hardware GPU Pass Duration

| Hint / Workload | Samples / Run | Baseline Allocator / PrivWS (MiB) | #11130 Allocator / PrivWS (MiB) | Δ Memory | Baseline CPU `p50` (min–max) | #11130 CPU `p50` (min–max) | Throughput Base vs #11130 | GPU Pass `p50` Base vs #11130 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `Performance` `idle` | — | 192.0 `[128, 64]` / 268.1 | **144.0** `[128, 16]` / **219.9** | **-48.0 / -48.2 MiB** | — | — | — | — |
| `Performance` `small_gui`* | 180 frames | 192.0 `[128, 64]` / 270.4 | **144.0** `[128, 16]` / **222.4** | **-48.0 / -48.0 MiB** | 479.5 us (452.9–522.0) | 469.6 us (451.0–582.6) | 1,976 vs 2,023 fps | — |
| `Performance` `repeated_uploads`* | 360 uploads | 192.0 `[128, 64]` / 270.7 | **144.0** `[128, 16]` / **222.7** | **-48.0 / -48.0 MiB** | 256.3 us (236.5–443.5) | 257.5 us (229.9–444.9) | 3,640 vs 3,684 ops/s | — |
| `Performance` `multi_surface` | 30 frames | 192.0 `[128, 64]` / 269.4 | **144.0** `[128, 16]` / **221.2** | **-48.0 / -48.2 MiB** | 11.07 ms (11.04–11.13) | 11.13 ms (11.04–11.15) | 97.8 vs 96.6 fps | — |
| `Performance` `churn` | 225 allocs | 192.0 `[128, 64]` / 270.2 | **144.0** `[128, 16]` / **222.1** | **-48.0 / -48.1 MiB** | 4.6 us (3.4–10.4) | 4.5 us (4.2–8.9) | 193k vs 144k ops/s† | — |
| `Performance` `sustained_render` | 225 passes | 256.0 `[128, 64×2]` / 334.2 | **208.0** `[128, 64, 16]` / **286.4** | **-48.0 / -47.8 MiB** | 3.93 ms (3.90–4.01) | 3.96 ms (3.90–4.02) | 252.8 vs 250.7 pass/s | **3,563.1** (3,493–3,615) vs **3,567.0 us** (3,494–3,608) |
| `Performance` `sustained_compute` | 105 dispatches | 256.0 `[128, 64×2]` / 334.9 | **208.0** `[128, 64, 16]` / **286.9** | **-48.0 / -48.0 MiB** | 853.3 us (834.6–925.3) | 837.9 us (816.3–853.4) | 1,138 vs 1,177 disp/s | **527.3** (519–531) vs **522.9 us** (520–527) |
| `Performance` `large_textures` | 20 × 16 MiB | 448.0 `[256, 128, 64]` / 544.5 | **400.0** `[256, 128, 16]` / **496.6** | **-48.0 / -47.9 MiB** | 1.96 ms (1.89–2.14) | 2.05 ms (1.81–2.91) | 327.6 vs 319.5 tex/s | — |
| `Performance` `large_alloc` | 5 buffers | 1004.0 / 1088.4 | **956.0** / **1040.5** | **-48.0 / -47.9 MiB** | 36.89 ms (20.44–55.76) | 21.67 ms (19.34–34.73) | 21.6 vs 36.7 ops/s | — |
| `MemoryUsage` `idle` | — | 12.0 `[8, 4]` / 86.9 | 12.0 `[8, 4]` / 87.1 | +0.0 / +0.2 MiB | — | — | — | — |
| `MemoryUsage` `small_gui` | 180 frames | 28.0 `[16, 8, 4]` / 105.7 | 28.0 `[16, 8, 4]` / 105.6 | +0.0 / -0.1 MiB | 628.5 us (527.9–638.1) | 463.8 us (444.8–601.9) | 1,550 vs 2,060 fps | — |

† *`churn` does sub-5 us GPU-only buffer alloc/free (total ~1–2 ms/run); mean throughput variance reflects occasional 40–50 us OS scheduling outliers (`p50` is `4.6 vs 4.5 us`, `p99` `12.2 vs 12.9 us`).*

- Across all 9 DX12 `Performance` workloads, allocator-reserved memory, DXGI Local Usage, Private Working Set, and OS Process Commit each drop by **~48.0 MiB** (bringing DX12 to exact `[128, 16] = 144 MiB` parity with Vulkan's transient pool), while CPU and hardware GPU pass timings stay within noise across every workload.
- **Hardware/platform limitations**: Local benchmarks were measured on an Intel Arc integrated (UMA) GPU on Windows 11; discrete DX12 GPUs (separate `L1` VRAM vs `L0` system RAM) and AMD/NVIDIA drivers were not benchmarked locally.

## Testing

- **Permanent GPU regression test**: Extended `TRANSIENT_BUFFERS_RELEASE_MEMORY_BLOCKS` in `tests/tests/wgpu-gpu/transient_memory.rs` to run on `Backends::DX12` alongside `Backends::VULKAN` (verifies `MemoryFlags::TRANSIENT` buffers do not share blocks with long-lived buffers and return their blocks on release; passes in Windows CI).
- **Unit & local checks**:
  - `cargo fmt --check -p wgpu-hal -p wgpu-test`: pass
  - `cargo clippy -p wgpu-hal --features dx12,vulkan --all-targets -- -D warnings` & `cargo clippy -p wgpu-test --test wgpu-gpu -- -D warnings`: pass
  - `cargo test -p wgpu-hal --features dx12,vulkan --lib`: 24/24 pass (including `allocation_sizes_tests::transient_sizes_quarter_and_clamp_to_minimum`)

## Squash or Rebase?

Single commit; ready to rebase onto `trunk`.

## LLM Use?

An AI coding agent investigated DX12 vs Vulkan memory allocation parity, implemented this change and enabled the DX12 `transient_memory` test, ran an independent review, executed the isolated local benchmarks, and wrote this PR description under explicit contributor authorization.
